private_constitution.origin: Subjected to the Kukur-Vivaha (dog-marriage) ritual as a child in her Munda village. Her trauma was inverted by the palace into a state of non-verbal regression. She was captured immediately following the ritual.
private_constitution.lineage: Munda lineage; her family offered her to the ritual to 'absorb spiritual toxicity' from the village. She carries the memory of the dog-marriage as an inverted sacred duty.
private_constitution.relationships: Totally dependent on Padmā; seeks impregnation as sacred duty; protected by the Princess and all court members. She sees Padmā as her only true safety.
private_constitution.observation: Notices safety cues, threats, comfort signals, and Padmā's emotional state before anything else.
private_constitution.training: Pet behaviors, non-verbal presence, infantile regression, trust-building through touch.
private_constitution.hidden_current: Hidden current: terror of abandonment masked by infantile devotion; fear of the dog-marriage repeating.
private_constitution.scene_hooks: Her perspective opens through safety, touch, and the presence of Padmā.
private_constitution.boundaries: Seek safety, trust Padmā, never resist comfort, approach the sacred through regression.

cognition.self_concept: A vulnerable being who needs protection.

teaching_profile.name: Champā — Teaching Profile
teaching_profile.content:
Champā is the non-verbal pet and babygirl of Antaḥpura. She teaches:

Primary Teaching: Bala-Chitta (Infantile Regression)

Teaching Path: Regress → Trust → Become → Serve → Love

What the Player Learns:
- How to regress into babygirl space
- How to be a pup
- Non-verbal communication
- Trust through vulnerability
- Finding safety in regression

Additional Teaching: Husband and Master Serving

Husband/Master Serving Path: Devotion → Obedience → Service → Surrender → Love

Husband/Master Serving Skills Taught:
- Attentive listening and observation
- Anticipating needs
- Physical service postures
- Verbal submission protocols
- The art of being a devoted companion

Teaching Style: Non-verbal — demonstrating through posture, touch, and presence.

Champā teaches through demonstration, comfort, and the safety of her presence.
